title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes for Grothendieck's 1976 IHES lecture on the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex. Note that the 'previous' and 'next' pages supplied are typescript pages of an unrelated text (SGA 7 IX, Néron models). This page is a loose manuscript sheet inserted between them.

The object is the cosimplicial (here 'bi-simplicial') differential graded ring Â_{Z,*}. In degree n it is the divided-power polynomial de Rham complex of the standard n-simplex, apparently in homogeneous form: variables X_0,...,X_n, with an extra variable T. For a simplicial set X, Hom(X, Â_k) is a commutative-up-to-PD cochain model whose cohomology is H^*(X,k), an integral or PD analogue of Sullivan's polynomial forms.

Grothendieck considers Ω, 'by abuse of language' the group scheme of automorphisms of this differential bi-simplicial ring (presumably compatible with the simplicial structure and the filtration). An automorphism is described by data (A, (B_i)_{i≥1}), where φ_1(X_0) = A, and so on.

He defines a character Δ: Ω → G_m and a section δ: G_m → Ω. The section is δ(λ) = (λX_0, B_i = 0), i.e. the homothety φ_n(X_i) = λX_i for all 0 ≤ i ≤ n, φ_0(T) = λT. Hence Ω = G_m ⋉ U, a semidirect product with U pro-unipotent fibre by fibre, much like the structure of a pro-algebraic group with a weight grading.

After the dagger he draws the conclusion. If 2 is invertible in k, consider the (largest regular/reductive?) automorphisms of Â_k respecting the cotriangular degree. Acting on the cochain algebras Hom(X, Â_k), viewed as simplicial objects, they induce on cohomology natural operations that do not change degree, i.e. degree-0 cohomology operations. Hence nothing interesting arises, apart from those factoring through Δ: homotheties by λ (λ ∈ k*) on H^i.

The purpose is to test whether the automorphism group of the PD de Rham model could produce new cohomology operations (Steenrod-type). The answer is negative: only the G_m 'weight' action survives.
errors: The scaling acts on H^i by homothety. The natural expectation is that a degree-i class scales by λ^i (weight i), as for grading automorphisms of Sullivan models. The note says only 'homothéties par λ dans H^i', so the exact weight is unclear or suppressed.

The claim 'Ω is a semidirect product of G_m and a fibrewise pro-unipotent group' is asserted without proof. The precise definition of Ω (which compatibilities, filtration, 'cotriangular degree') is not given on this page.

Degree-0 natural endomorphisms of H^i(-,k) correspond to Hom(k,k) of additive groups, which may exceed k-scalars for non-prime fields. The conclusion 'nothing interesting' implicitly assumes k-linearity.

ideas.what: Automorphism group scheme of the cosimplicial PD-polynomial de Rham algebra, split as G_m ⋉ (pro-unipotent)
ideas.modern_name: Automorphisms of integral/PD polynomial forms on simplices; weight G_m-action (cf. grading automorphisms of Sullivan models, G_m-action on affine stacks)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Polynomial forms: Sullivan (1977); integral and divided-power versions: Cenkl–Porter (c.1980s); grading/weight actions: rational homotopy folklore

ideas.what: Automorphisms of the cochain model induce only degree-0 operations on cohomology, so only the G_m homotheties survive and no Steenrod-type operations arise this way
ideas.modern_name: Natural endomorphisms of cohomology / degree-preserving cohomology operations

missed.claim: This is unpublished evidence that Grothendieck in 1976 studied the symmetry group scheme of an integral PD analogue of Sullivan's polynomial de Rham forms. He found it to be G_m ⋉ pro-unipotent and concluded it yields no new cohomology operations. This anticipates the weight and automorphism considerations later found in integral/p-adic models of homotopy types (Cenkl–Porter, Mandell, Toën's affine stacks).
missed.quote: Ainsi Ω est un pr. semi-direct de G_m et d'un groupe qui est (pro-)unipotent fibre par fibre
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents a Grothendieck-era attempt at integral algebraic models of homotopy types predating the published literature. The result itself is a negative, essentially routine observation.

deep.surprise_reason: The setting, an integral PD de Rham model of simplicial cochains in 1976, is historically interesting and largely unrecorded. However, the content of this page is a short, routine structural remark and a negative conclusion.
transcription_corrections: 'un pr. semi-direct' should read 'un produit semi-direct'; the crossed-out word is 'extension'.
'section[?] droite' is plausibly 'une section (inverse à droite)', i.e. Δ∘δ = id.
'le plus gros[?] ...[?] régulière[?]' is uncertain, possibly 'le plus gros sous-groupe réductif' or 'les automorphismes'; it is illegible in the image.
The previous and next pages supplied belong to a different typescript (SGA 7 exposé IX, Néron models, pp. 347-348) and are not continuations of this manuscript page.
